name: RAG-MCP: Mitigating Prompt Bloat in LLM Tool Selection via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors_affiliation: Tiantian Gan and Qiyao Sun. Affiliations listed as Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (Beijing, China) and Queen Mary University of London (London, UK); contact emails are QMUL (jp2022213034@qmul.ac.uk, jp2022213402@qmul.ac.uk).
code_url: N/A (no official code repository released by the authors; the paper relies on the publicly released MCPBench / 'Evaluation Report on MCP Servers' (arXiv:2504.11094) framework and WebSearch dataset, which it credits in the acknowledgements. Third-party GitHub repos named 'rag-mcp' are unrelated.)
task_domain: tool-use (LLM external tool / MCP-server selection and invocation), with web-search tasks as the evaluation setting.
problem_setting: Interactive single-agent tool use: an LLM agent must, for a natural-language query, select and invoke the correct external tool from a large registry of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. The core problem is 'prompt bloat' and decision overhead when the number of available tools scales to hundreds or thousands - including all tool schemas in the prompt saturates the context window with distractors and degrades selection accuracy. The setting is test-time / inference (no LLM fine-tuning); each trial allows up to 10 rounds of interaction with MCP servers. The toolset is large/open and can grow (new MCPs added by indexing). Supervision: a ground-truth MCP is defined per task for accuracy measurement, but the retriever itself is off-the-shelf (no task-specific training).
what_is_retrieved: tools (MCP server schemas / function descriptions, including tool-use parameters, metadata, and usage examples).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: an external vector index built over MCP server metadata drawn from a registry of 4,400+ publicly listed MCP servers (mcp.so). The index can be extended by adding new MCP metadata, but it is not a growing/episodic memory the agent writes to during task execution.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Top-k ranking objective collapsed to top-1 in practice: the retriever returns top-k candidate MCPs but only the single best (top-1) MCP schema is injected into the LLM prompt for execution. The evaluation targets selecting the one ground-truth tool, not recovering a complete multi-tool set.
retrieval_unit: tool-API: a single MCP server description / function schema (problem-relevant tool metadata including parameters and usage examples).
index_source: Static, offline-constructed retrievable store: an external vector index over MCP metadata from a registry of 4,400+ publicly listed MCP servers; extensible by indexing new MCPs without retraining, but not induced online/test-time.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index (semantic vector-space index of MCP descriptions). No graph/hierarchical organization in this work; authors note future work on hierarchical indexes for extreme scale.
retriever_type: Dense semantic retriever described as an LLM-based encoder/retriever (uses Qwen / qwen-max-0125 to encode the user query) performing semantic vector search over the MCP index. Best characterized as dense / LLM-as-encoder semantic retrieval.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf): the retriever uses semantic similarity over embeddings of an existing LLM encoder (Qwen-max); no contrastive training, no LM-feedback, and no RL/preference learning of the retriever is described.
query_construction: Raw input: the user's natural-language task description is encoded (with Qwen-max) and used directly as the query for semantic search over the MCP index. No decomposition, expansion, or synthetic query reformulation is described.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): the query is constructed once from the user's task description before LLM engagement.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: a single retrieval step is performed before engaging the LLM for execution (tool discovery is decoupled from generation and done up front).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always invoked once per query at the start of the pipeline (before the LLM), not gated by any confidence/uncertainty/reflection signal.
reranking: Candidates are ranked by semantic similarity and an optional Validation step can generate a few-shot example query per retrieved MCP and test its response as a 'sanity check' before invocation; this functions as a lightweight validation/filter rather than a learned cross-encoder reranker. No dedicated cross-encoder or RRF reranking stage is described.
retrieved_context_refinement: Selection/truncation plus optional validation: from the top-k retrieved MCPs, only the single best MCP schema is injected (focused context filtering); the optional validation step (synthetic few-shot test of each candidate) acts as a basic compatibility check. No reason-in-documents distillation or compression beyond top-1 selection.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: only the selected (top-1) MCP's schema and tool-use parameters are injected into the LLM prompt / function-calling API, which then plans and executes the task without needing to discover tools.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan (tool discovery decoupled from generation): a single up-front retrieval narrows the toolset, then the LLM performs planning and execution (up to 10 interaction rounds with the chosen MCP) using only the selected tool. Retrieval is not interleaved per step nor embedded in a tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-task: retrieval happens once before the reasoning/execution phase; it is not woven per-CoT-step or per-tool-call within the rollout.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw tool schema / metadata: the injected surface form is the MCP function description, parameters, and usage examples (structured tool documentation), not a distilled strategy, free-text workflow, or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Procedural tool / API specification (a single concrete tool schema). It is an actionable tool description rather than a raw trajectory, distilled strategy, or hint.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Focused context filtering (inject only the single most relevant MCP, avoiding distractor tool descriptions) plus an optional pre-invocation Validation step (synthetic few-shot test of retrieved candidates). No retriever-aware training or distractor-aware SFT; robustness comes from reducing the candidate set rather than training-time defenses.
memory_type: none (static external tool index; no episodic/skill/workflow memory written by the agent). The MCP index is a static, extensible knowledge store rather than a learned memory.
write_back: False - the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills from task execution. New MCPs can be added to the index by manual indexing of their metadata, but this is index maintenance, not agent write-back of trajectories or outcomes.
online_growth: No automatic online growth from deployment experience. The store is extensible (new MCP metadata can be indexed without retraining), but it does not grow from the agent's own task interactions at test time.
write_back_trigger: Never (no experience/case write-back occurs during deployment). Index updates, when they happen, are external/manual additions of new MCP metadata, not triggered by task success or failure.
failure_experience_usage: None: failed or negative experiences are not stored or retrieved. The framework does not maintain success vs failure cases; it only diagnoses failure via the stress test analysis (no corrective memory).
memory_evolution_update: Append-only at the index level (new MCP metadata can be added); stored entries are not mutated, merged, refined, or pruned by the system. No experience-driven evolution.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval is a fixed similarity-based top-k (top-1) semantic selection, not a learned/RL-optimized policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-agent setting with a private/shared static tool index; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing is described.
benchmarks: (1) MCP stress test on WebSearch tasks - a custom Needle-in-a-Haystack-style test varying the candidate MCP pool size N from 1 to 11100 (across 26 intervals), with one ground-truth MCP and N-1 distractors drawn from a registry of 4,400+ MCP servers (mcp.so), using 20 web-search tasks. (2) The web-search subset of MCPBench (from 'Evaluation Report on MCP Servers', arXiv:2504.11094) used as a held-out testbed, with 20 independent trials per baseline (success = >10/20 correct).
benchmark_family: tool (MCP tool selection/invocation; MCPBench web-search subset) plus a custom long-context-style 'MCP stress test' inspired by Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH).
baselines: Three selection strategies compared: (1) Blank Conditioning ('Blank') - prompt the LLM with all N MCP descriptions at once; (2) Actual Match - keyword pre-filtering of the candidate pool on task description/MCP metadata, then prompt on the reduced set; (3) RAG-MCP (the proposed method) - vector-index semantic retriever injecting only the top candidate's schema.
key_metrics: Accuracy (%) = percentage of trials selecting the ground-truth MCP; Avg Prompt Tokens; Avg Completion Tokens. The stress test additionally reports per-trial selection accuracy / task success vs MCP pool size N (and mentions latency). Answer correctness automated via Deepseek-v3 as evaluator (text also mentions a 'Llama as Judge' verifier).
headline_result: On the MCPBench web-search subset, RAG-MCP achieves 43.13% accuracy vs 13.62% for Blank Conditioning (more than triple) and 18.20% for Actual Match, while cutting average prompt tokens to 1084.00 vs 2133.84 for Blank (a >50% / roughly half reduction). Completion tokens: RAG-MCP 78.14 vs Blank 162.25 vs Actual Match 23.60.
ablations: No formal component ablation table. The main comparative study (RAG-MCP vs Blank Conditioning vs Actual Match) isolates the contribution of semantic retrieval+top-1 injection over naive all-tools prompting and keyword pre-filtering. The MCP stress test serves as a scaling analysis (varying pool size N from 1 to 11100), showing high success below ~30 MCPs, mid-range variability at positions 31-70, and degradation beyond ~100 MCPs, demonstrating that retrieval precision drops as the registry scales.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial: selection Accuracy (an intrinsic tool-selection metric, fraction of trials choosing the ground-truth MCP) is reported alongside token-usage and task success. There is no separate Recall@k / nDCG / completeness reporting decoupled from end-to-end success; accuracy doubles as both selection correctness and the primary outcome.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-oriented (selection accuracy and task success), with token-usage efficiency reported. The stress test adds a coarse process view (per-trial success across MCP positions / pool sizes), but no reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise process scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: RAG-MCP roughly halves prompt tokens (1084.00 vs 2133.84 for Blank, abstract cites '>50%' reduction) while raising accuracy from 13.62% to 43.13%. Completion tokens increase vs Actual Match (78.14 vs 23.60), framed as a beneficial trade-off correlating with higher accuracy. The paper also argues resource efficiency by activating only the selected MCP server (not instantiating all registered servers), lowering startup cost; it mentions measuring latency in the stress test but reports no concrete latency numbers.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Reranked-then-truncated to top-1: the retriever returns top-k candidates but only the single best MCP schema is injected into the prompt, capping injected-tool context to one tool description (k effectively = 1 at injection). No explicit token budget cap beyond this top-1 selection.
builds_on: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al., 2020) as the core retrieve-then-generate principle; Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP, 2024) as the tool-integration standard; Gorilla (Patil et al., 2024) which retrieves API documentation to improve API-call generation; the RAG survey (Gao et al., 2023). Evaluation builds directly on MCPBench / 'Evaluation Report on MCP Servers' (Luo et al., 2025, arXiv:2504.11094) code framework and WebSearch dataset. Stress test inspired by the Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH) test.
contrasts_with: Naive all-tools prompting / conventional MCP clients (e.g., Claude or early GPT-4 integrations) that instantiate and present all registered tools at once ('Blank Conditioning'); keyword-based pre-filtering ('Actual Match'); prompt-based tool-use methods such as ReAct and model-tuning methods such as Toolformer and WebGPT that do not address tool-discovery at scale.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). Part of the tool/MCP-retrieval lineage that treats large-scale tool discovery as a retrieval subproblem (descending from Gorilla-style API-doc retrieval and classic RAG), applying it to the emerging MCP ecosystem to mitigate prompt bloat as tool counts scale.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle - it retrieves static tool schemas, not problem-solution cases).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is framed purely as retrieval-augmented tool selection.
tool_document_engineering: Raw tool metadata embeddings: each MCP's description/schema (with parameters and usage examples) is represented in a vector space using an LLM encoder (Qwen-max). No synthetic-query augmentation, summary expansion, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings are described; an optional validation step generates a few-shot test query per candidate at retrieval time rather than for index construction.
index_content_separation: Partial / implicit: tool discovery is decoupled from generation and only the selected MCP's full schema+parameters are loaded into the prompt on demand (lightweight semantic index over metadata, heavier schema injected only for the chosen tool). This resembles progressive disclosure but is not explicitly framed as a separated index-then-content design.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Protocol: Model Context Protocol (MCP) - tools are MCP server schemas invoked via the function-calling interface. The index is a static external vector store extensible by manually indexing new MCP metadata; no live CRUD auto-synchronization with the MCP registry is described (index updates are manual, not automatic live sync).
tool_dependency_awareness: No: retrieval treats each MCP independently and selects a single tool; inter-tool dependencies, shared auth, prerequisites, or dependency graphs are not modeled. Multi-tool workflows are listed as future work.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR case adaptation; the retrieved tool schema is used as-is for function calling).
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey/taxonomy).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Not a benchmark paper, but it constructs a custom MCP stress test: candidate pool size N varied from 1 to 11100 across 26 intervals, one ground-truth MCP plus N-1 distractors sampled from a registry of 4,400+ publicly listed MCP servers (mcp.so), evaluated on 20 web-search tasks; correctness auto-judged by Deepseek-v3 (and a 'Llama as Judge' verifier mentioned). The end-to-end comparison uses the MCPBench web-search subset (arXiv:2504.11094) with 20 trials per baseline; best system (RAG-MCP) reaches 43.13% accuracy, signaling the task remains difficult.
